palette: Shared sound palette for the whole game: glockenspiel, celesta, marimba, sleigh bells, soft felt piano, warm toy brass, plucky bass, wooden toy percussion, and puffy snow foley. Cozy, warm, toy-like winter; never harsh, metallic, realistic or scary.
style: One consistent set: every sound must feel like it comes from the same world. Use the shared palette. Tonal sounds in D major (the North, boss and finale music in D minor). Effects are short and dry (no big reverb, a small room at most), start instantly with no silence at the front, and contain no music or voices unless the item asks for them.
voice: One voice for all six lines: a cheerful, bright, friendly cartoon announcer, excited but never shouty, cleared for commercial use (never a copy of a real person). Each line under 1 second, no music or effects behind it.
rights: Use a Fish Audio paid plan: paid plans include commercial rights; the free tier's terms aren't stated.
order: 1) the 8 priority-A effects, then send those to the account owner for Alex to hear in the game before going on; 2) the 6 voice lines (Fish Audio text to speech); 3) the B and C effects.

deliver.format: WAV, 44.1 kHz, 16-bit. WAV is lossless, and MP3 adds silence at the start and end that breaks seamless loops. The game's final MP3s are made from these.
deliver.takes: Deliver every take, numbered: <name>_1.wav, <name>_2.wav, <name>_3.wav. Don't pick a favourite; we choose by listening in the game.
deliver.manifest: manifest.csv in the zip root, one row per file: file,type,take,seconds_actual,prompt_used,notes
deliver.problems: If the tool can't make an item exactly as written, stop and tell the account owner. Don't swap in something else.

items.name: sweep
items.when: CLEAN SWEEP! at 98%: the last snow melts away in a ring and the job ends.
items.prompt: Magical cozy winter sweep: a soft rising whoosh of powdery snow swirling outward, ending in a bright sparkling glockenspiel arpeggio in D major, cheerful toy-like video game reward, dry, no reverb tail, the sound happens right at the start, then silence

items.name: treasure
items.when: Finding a treasure in the snow.
items.prompt: Treasure discovered: a warm music box and glockenspiel flourish rising in D major with a sparkle at the end, cozy winter, toy-like, short and joyful, no reverb tail, the sound happens right at the start, then silence

items.name: pow
items.when: The punch under a crash (plays on top of the bump sound).
items.prompt: Short cartoon impact thump, soft and puffy like crashing into a big snowbank, with a quick muffled pop, toy-like and playful, not violent, very short, no reverb, the sound happens right at the start, then silence

items.name: swipe
items.when: Jobs, Upgrades and Garage pages sliding across.
items.prompt: Very short soft swipe whoosh, like a card sliding quickly across a table, airy and light, subtle UI sound, no click, the sound happens right at the start, then silence

items.name: bookopen
items.when: Opening the Treasure Book.
items.prompt: Old leather-bound book opening: a soft leather creak and a gentle paper flutter, cozy, close-up, short, dry, the sound happens right at the start, then silence

items.name: crack

items.prompt: Small cartoon ice crack: a quick crisp crackle of thin ice with a tiny falling two-note blip, light and playful, a warning not a failure, very short, dry, the sound happens right at the start, then silence

items.prompt: Exciting transformation: a quick rising whoosh into a big cartoon engine rev with a bright sparkle at the top, energetic but cozy and toy-like, video game power-up, no voice, dry, the sound happens right at the start, then silence

lengths: Fish Audio takes whole seconds (1 s minimum). Ask for request_seconds; the sound plays at the very start and the rest is silence. Deliver it untrimmed: it's trimmed to trim_to when it goes into the game.
music: Not made in Fish Audio (its generator does ambience, foley and impacts, not music). The music is made separately.
takes: One take per sound. A second take only for a sound that comes back wrong, and only after the account owner OKs it.
budget: Hard limit 1,000,000 Fish credits for the whole game; use as few as possible. Quote each batch before generating.
